subject.title: feat: expose rawBody on user messages in plugin hook events

question: Should OpenClaw accept `rawBody?: string` as the plugin hook contract for `before_prompt_build`, legacy `before_agent_start`, and `agent_end`, including the documented direct-user and steer semantics?
rationale: Code review can verify the plumbing, but this is a new external plugin API and security-boundary contract that maintainers must choose rather than automation inferring the permanent surface.

options.title: Accept after ordering fix
options.body: Keep the `rawBody` API, require the active-run delivery-order repair and rebase, then review the exact head for merge.

options.title: Defer to trusted inbound contract
options.body: Pause this PR and fold hook raw input into the broader trusted inbound-decoration design in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/95333.

options.title: Reject this API shape
options.body: Close or redirect the PR if maintainers do not want clean direct-user text exposed directly on these hook events.

recommendation.title: Accept after ordering fix
recommendation.body: Keep the `rawBody` API, require the active-run delivery-order repair and rebase, then review the exact head for merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history connects this owner to Codex and embedded agent runtime work, and the decision spans runtime behavior plus plugin API direction.
